questions.stem: Where does most selective reabsorption take place in the nephron?
questions.explanation: The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) is the main site of selective reabsorption. Its cells have many microvilli to increase surface area and many mitochondria to provide energy for active transport.

questions.stem: How is glucose reabsorbed from the filtrate back into the blood?

options.text: By active transport using energy from ATP
By diffusion through the cell membrane
By osmosis down a concentration gradient

questions.explanation: Glucose is reabsorbed from the filtrate by active transport, which requires energy from ATP. This allows all glucose to be reabsorbed against a concentration gradient, so none is normally lost in urine.

questions.stem: What percentage of filtered water is typically reabsorbed by the nephron?
questions.explanation: Approximately 99% of filtered water is reabsorbed. Of the roughly 180 litres filtered daily, only about 1-2 litres is excreted as urine. Water is reabsorbed by osmosis, following the reabsorption of solutes.

questions.stem: Why do the cells of the proximal convoluted tubule have many mitochondria?

options.text: To provide energy for active transport of substances like glucose
To break down proteins into amino acids
To generate the pressure needed for ultrafiltration

questions.explanation: The many mitochondria in PCT cells carry out aerobic respiration to produce ATP. This energy is needed to power active transport, which moves glucose, amino acids, and other useful molecules back into the blood against concentration gradients.

questions.stem: Which substance is only partially reabsorbed, with about 50% remaining in the filtrate to be excreted?
questions.explanation: About 50% of urea is passively reabsorbed by diffusion, while the rest remains in the filtrate and is excreted in urine. Unlike glucose and amino acids, which are 100% reabsorbed, urea is a waste product that the body needs to remove.

questions.stem: Why is the process called 'selective' reabsorption?

options.text: Because the process only occurs when the body needs water
Because reabsorption only happens during the day
Because only certain useful substances are reabsorbed while waste products are left behind
Because only the right kidney performs reabsorption

questions.explanation: It is called 'selective' because the nephron reabsorbs specific useful substances (like glucose and amino acids) back into the blood while leaving waste products (like urea) in the filtrate to be excreted. Different substances are reabsorbed in different amounts.

questions.stem: By which process is water reabsorbed from the filtrate?
questions.explanation: Water is reabsorbed by osmosis. As solutes (glucose, salts, amino acids) are actively reabsorbed into the blood, the water potential of the blood decreases, causing water to follow by osmosis from the filtrate into the surrounding capillaries.
